text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a spike in GPU pod launch failures in us-west1 over the last hour. Root cause points to local NVMe IO errors when the scrubber runs
raj: yup saw that. many nodes stuck in Provisioning -> Attach awaiting disk readiness
alex: correlated with nightly deep-scrub window kicking in. scrub concurrency hit all local nvme devices at once :grimacing:
maya: paste of kernel messages from one host:
```
[ 1250.234567] nvme0: I/O 0xabcdef timeout, status: 0x2
[ 1250.234590] nvme0: retrying command
[ 1251.345678] nvme0: failed command status: medium error
[ 1251.345700] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
```
tanya: also noticed spike in blockstore proxy latency around same time — nodes report long waits attaching encrypted ephemeral volumes
ops-jen: scrub job config currently set to `concurrency: 28` per-region for us-west1. we ramped it up last month to catch wear faster after the fleet refresh
kyle: the fleet refresh increased smaller new nvme counts; those drives have higher write amplification early in life, so aggressive scrub + batch GPU launches = bad combo
maya: any quick mitigations? we have GPU queues piling up and preemptible offers are being rejected because nodes never become Ready
raj: temp mitigation = scale down scrub concurrency to 8 and stagger start times by AZ. also throttle janitor IO to `ionice -c3` on scrub processes
alex: agreed. i'm pushing a small roll (us-west1 scrub policy) — will defer deep-scrub for nodes with pending gpu-allocs
ops-jen: patch suggestion for scrub policy:
```yaml
scrub:
  concurrency: "8"
  start-window: "03:00-07:00,09:00-11:00,22:00-23:59"
  io-priority: "low"
  skip-if-pending-gpu: true
```
kyle: note this will increase wear monitoring backlog and some devices will stay flagged longer, cost vs availability tradeoff
tanya: storage-proxy team is rerouting a subset of attach traffic to the standby cluster — should reduce latency in ~10m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: #INC-2026-217 — nvme-scrub-throttle-causing-gpu-launch-failures (severity: medium). Pager on-call: raj
maya: thanks. who wants action on communication to sales/customer success for affected accounts (some high-throughput customers in us-west1)?
raj: i'll draft a short note, cc ops-jen. we should avoid saying "nvme scrub" in customer emails; keep it high-level: "storage maintenance caused provisioning delay"
ops-jen: after we stabilize, let's run a small experiment: reduce scrub concurrency cluster-wide for 6 hours and measure GPU attach latency + failed pod counts
alex: i'll add a metric on the rollout dashboard: `gpu_attach_fail_rate` + `nvme_attach_latency_p95` and tag by scrub-policy-version
maya: sounds good. timeline?
kyle: mitigation rollout in 5m, monitor 30m, rollback if failures > 2x baseline
maya: thanks team. update here in 30m with metrics. :thumbsup:
